frontierMethod: The curve comes from simulating every panel-and-battery combination on a coarse grid against the same hourly weather as the cards above, then keeping only the systems nothing cheaper beats. Prices use the same landed do-it-yourself middle as every other figure on this page.
frontierMethodBattery: The curve comes from simulating every battery size on a coarse grid against the same hourly weather and tariff windows as the cards above, then keeping only the systems nothing cheaper beats. Panels are not part of this run, so the curve varies the bank alone. Prices use the same landed do-it-yourself middle as every other figure on this page.

sizingSectionIntro: Enter your location and average electric bill. We simulate 5 years of hourly NASA satellite weather to size the exact solar panel array and battery storage you need — with honest 20-year payback, battery replacement cadence, and equipment costs in your local currency.
quickModeLabel: {control}⚡ Quick setup — choose inputs, then click Size My System
locationLookupHelp: The precise-location button fills your exact coordinates and pulls area prices from the nearest reference region. For another place, type a city or town and press Enter or Tab to resolve it. Then click Size My System to calculate.
mapPrivacyNote: Satellite imagery (no account needed) loads only after you ask for it. Coordinates go to the map tiles and NASA weather; nothing is saved.
exactLocationHelp: A city lookup is convenient, but your exact location gives the most precise weather and solar estimate. Enter custom latitude and longitude manually, or use Use my current location for browser GPS.

generatorFuelAssumption: Assumes a small genset at typical partial load: petrol {petrolBurn}{petrolUnit}, diesel {dieselBurn}{dieselUnit} (fuel only — oil, filters, and engine wear push the true number higher). If you know your real $/kWh, type it directly instead.
feedInCreditLabel: Feed-in credit for surplus you can sell ($/kWh, optional — grid-tie only):
fixedMonthlyChargeLabel: Fixed monthly charge on your bill ($/mo, optional — solar can't cut it):
applianceWattageNote: Wattages are typical values — yours may differ. Cycling appliances (fridges, freezers, air conditioners, pumps) only draw power while running: their slider is hours actually running per day, capped to realistic compressor time, and each row shows the resulting 24-hour average. A modern fridge at the default (100 W running, ~10 h/day) really does use about 1 kWh/day.
billTotalsNote: Bills include fixed charges and taxes, so this slightly overestimates real use — which is a safe direction to err.
roofAreaHelp: A rough manual estimate is enough: about 6 m² per 400 W panel. This only caps the searched solar size; leave it blank for the normal estimate. Your coordinates are never stored.

surplusSizingHelp: Above 100% the system is sized to produce sellable surplus — without a feed-in credit entered above, that surplus has no cash value and is flagged as clipped waste. The “your target” matrix column and the price-cut curve follow this slider.
resultsIntro: Results appear here: a recommended path first, with battery comparisons and all options available below. For grid-tied plans, the result also separates bill reduction from outage backup.
bomSafetyNote: Educational estimate from your sizing result — not an engineering design, not a shopping order. Fuse and cable figures assume copper, conservative ampacity, and a short battery-to-inverter run; verify everything against your local electrical code with a licensed professional before buying or energizing anything.
calculationDetailsHelp: Run a sizing first - every constant used (derates, temperature model, efficiencies, weather data years and source) is listed here.
bomIntro: A reference parts list so you know what the pieces are and roughly what they cost. Nothing here is sold by this site — prices are indicative figures seen on the open market and change constantly.
bomCellsDescription: Brand new Grade-A prismatic LFP cells. 16S configuration per pack (51.2V nominal).
bomBmsDescription: Smart active balancing (2A balance current), dual temperature probes, RS485/CANbus comms with Sol-Ark & Victron.
bomFuseDescription: 20kA AIC interrupt rating @ 160V DC. Clears very high short-circuit DC currents in milliseconds — sized to protect the BMS and wiring.
bomRackDescription: Belleville spring washer endplates hold uniform compression (about 3,000 N). Manufacturers cite cycle-life benefits; treat specific gains as unverified.
faqIntro: Short answers to what people ask most. The AI advisor can go deeper on any of these.
faqAccuracyAnswer: Every number comes from testable code simulating your exact location against five years of NASA satellite weather — not an AI guessing. Real-world results still vary with shading, installation quality, and hardware, so have a licensed professional verify anything you build.
faqPaybackAnswer: Where grid power is expensive — Hawaii, islands, much of Europe, Africa, South Asia — properly built solar plus storage commonly repays its component cost in one to four years, then runs nearly free for decades. The calculator shows your personal payback from your own tariff.
faqCostAnswer: Battery banks self-built from prismatic cells typically land around $80–125 per usable kWh shipped and duty-paid; budget retail packs run roughly $110–165. Panels add about $0.16–0.38 per watt. Every result states its price scope honestly.
faqGeneratorAnswer: Only if you want near-total independence through weeks of bad weather. The three off-grid options show exactly that trade-off: one never needs a generator, one needs it about a day a year, one only now and then. Grid-connected users skip this entirely.
faqOfflineAnswer: Yes. After your first visit the tool installs itself as an offline app: sizing math runs entirely in your browser, and if the network is down it falls back to bundled typical-year weather for the nearest of 66 reference cities.
faqSafetyAnswer: It demands respect: lithium cells store enough energy to start fires, and DC arcs don't switch off. The guides here insist on proper fusing, BMS use, and code compliance — and on having a licensed electrician check anything before you energize it.
